acceptance: Two independent members and one dependent member land and produce one bound final PR.
The outsider server's take of an active member is refused.
A second landing with a stale integration head is refused, then succeeds after the member re-syncs and rechecks.
A declared same-file overlap lands and the earlier member's rerun is recorded; the silent-revert counterexample cannot reach passing final evidence.
A run killed after merge and before prepare resumes through batch-status without a second merge.
context_append on a prepared member keeps its receipt; an acceptance edit invalidates it.
A review fix after the PR opens is recorded as an advance and rebinds the PR; stale final evidence is refused until refreshed.
A conflicting develop change is merged in as a recorded develop-merge advance and readiness passes.
pr-open in a member worktree refuses before any side effect; abort_batch returns members to the ordinary lifecycle.
An ordinary single-item delivery is unchanged.
After the leader server is killed, a new server recovers batch ownership with the exact owner and generation, and batch-status continues the batch with no lost receipt.
Runs through a lock-taking entry point with no live cloud and no real model or omp calls; no scenario only checks wiring.
context:
Decision gate: start only after batch-land-and-status-20261101 and pr-landing-arm-batch-evidence-20261101 are done. Guardrails: deliver as an ordinary serial PR to develop (AGENTS.md: feature delivery cannot deliver the changes that make it possible); write only from a linked worktree made with make worktree-create and checked with make agent-write-preflight, never the primary clone; stage explicit paths, never git add -A; no explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001, make comment-policy-check); heavy test runs only through lock-taking entry points, never BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK; never weaken hold labels, the unresolved-thread refusal, oracle-gate, duration or suite gates; add a changelog.d fragment (CHANGELOG_INTERNAL when nothing is user-visible); durable artifacts carry no session or phase labels; cited line numbers are leads, so re-read the code before editing; tests prove behaviour, never wiring or wording.

Lands in the BenchBox core PR, so the proof exists before the pilot uses the loop.
description: Add a real-Git end-to-end scenario under tests/integration/worktree/ using an isolated tracker remote, two real todo-db-mcp servers (leader and outsider) and fake hosted responses, driving the batch targets as built. This is the proof before the pilot runs on real work.
